dek: New Terminal One slipped to 2027, so here's how to get to JFK and make your flight.

slides.label: The Truth
slides.text: Searching for the JFK new terminal opening date? Here's the answer: *neither new terminal is open* this Thanksgiving.

slides.label: Open Terminals
slides.text: You're flying out of Terminals 1, 4, 5, 7 or 8, through an airport that's still a *construction zone*.

slides.label: New Terminal One
slides.text: New Terminal One, once hoped for summer 2026, is now *expected in 2027*, with 23 gates when finished.

slides.label: Terminal 6
slides.text: Terminal 6 still lists 2026 on paper, but it's *not in JFK's terminal directory* right now. Don't expect to check in there.

slides.label: Roads & Pickup
slides.text: The $19 billion redevelopment means detours everywhere: Terminal 7 pickup moved *inside the parking garage*.

slides.label: Transit
slides.text: Every rail trip ends on the AirTrain. Take it to *Jamaica or Howard Beach*, the subway plus AirTrain runs $11.75.

slides.label: Parking & TSA
slides.text: *Pre-book parking 3 hours ahead.* No REAL ID? TSA's ConfirmID fee is $45, with no guarantee you get through.

slides.label: The Ask
slides.text: Leave early, take the train if you can, and have your ID and e-Ticket ready. *Your job is just to get to the table.*

JFK Thanksgiving travel 2026 means one truth up front: neither new terminal is open yet, so you're flying out of Terminals 1, 4, 5, 7 or 8 through a full construction zone.

New Terminal One, once hoped for summer 2026, is now expected in 2027. Terminal 6 still says 2026 online, but it's not even in JFK's own terminal directory right now. The $19 billion redevelopment means detours everywhere, from Terminal 7's pickup moving inside the parking garage to new ramps at Terminal 5.

Our job this holiday isn't to fix construction. It's to get you through it: which AirTrain stop to use, when to pre-book parking, what TSA's $45 ConfirmID fee means if you don't have a REAL ID, and how to pack the pie so it clears security.

Sound familiar? Every founder knows a launch date that quietly becomes a 'phase one.'

For anyone flying out of JFK this Thanksgiving, or anyone shipping a product on a deadline, the lesson is the same: build your plan around what's actually open, not what's promised.
